solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Production of Lear — the first of many in the area

indicators.note: a production of a play reworks the text, so the letters of Lear are reshaped
only the opening letter of many is wanted here

explanation.surface: A theatre review notes that a staging of King Lear is the first of many in the district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Production of' rearranges LEAR into REAL; 'the first of' gives M from many; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or field, a synonym for an area of activity or territory.

clue.text: Cream endlessly perform American smash

indicators.note: with both ends of the word cream removed, only its inner letters remain

parts.note: to render a song is to perform it

explanation.surface: A rock fan urges the band Cream, playing without end, to give an American hit a go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips both ends of CREAM, leaving REA. Cream was a British rock band, which suits the reading of 'smash' as a hit record.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear-ender is the American term for a collision where one car hits the back of another, a smash.

clue.text: Polygraph identified source of nuisance

indicators.note: the clue words polygraph identified serve as the source holding the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A lie detector test pinpoints who was causing the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across polygrAPH IDentified, with 'source of' signalling that those words supply it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are sap-sucking insects, a familiar garden pest and so a nuisance.

clue.text: Hopelessly romantic with no time for big name in radio

indicators.note: something done hopelessly is in disarray, signalling that the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is a hopeless romantic who never has time for the stars of the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes the T from ROMANTIC, leaving ROMANIC, and 'Hopelessly' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi pioneered long-distance wireless telegraphy, making him a celebrated figure in early broadcasting.

clue.text: Passionate about pub, shortly getting blurry

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for passionate wraps the short pub

parts.note: passionate in love means amorous
PH, for public house, is the short form of pub

explanation.surface: Ardent drinkers at the pub soon find their vision going fuzzy.
explanation.walkthrough: PH, for public house, is a convention solvers may not know; 'getting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorphous means without clear shape or form, close to blurry or ill-defined.

clue.text: River Thames is empty following bitter warnings

indicators.note: following places the river and Thames pieces after the bitter

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer, an ale

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its outside letters, so Thames loses its middle

explanation.surface: Drought alerts are issued because the Thames has run dry after a bitter spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is empty' strips the inside of Thames, and 'following' puts the river and Thames pieces after the drink. Bitter is a hoppy British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerts are signals of danger, the same thing as warnings.

clue.text: Completely expose Conservatives?

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them publicly
conservatives in politics are the right wing

explanation.surface: A journalist wonders whether to unmask the whole Tory party.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means wholly and without reservation, a synonym of completely.

clue.text: Front of horse in Christmas show followed by James Bond character in musical?

indicators.note: followed by sets the Bond character after the earlier pieces
in puts the front of horse inside the word for the Christmas show

parts.note: a panto, or pantomime, is a British family stage show put on at Christmas

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A Christmas pantomime horse appears, followed by a Bond figure, in what sounds like a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime horse is a two-person costume, so 'front of horse' reads naturally; it gives H, which goes into PANTO. The question mark signals a definition by example: The Phantom of the Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phantom of the Opera is a famous musical, often just called Phantom, so the clue defines by example.

clue.text: Timely piano in poor composition and melody

indicators.note: in puts the piano letter inside the rearranged poor
a composition is something put together, so the letters of poor are reassembled

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
a melody is a tune

explanation.surface: A timely piano piece is let down by a poor composition and its melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges the letters of poor into OPOR before the piano letter goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means well-timed or coming at a convenient moment, matching timely.

clue.text: Half past eight start in the morning creates a kind of pressure

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word past, here its second pair of letters
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks a morning time

explanation.surface: Getting going at half past eight in the morning puts one under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes ST, the back half of PAST; 'start' gives E from eight; 'creates' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam pressure is the force of compressed vapour, as in a steam engine or boiler.

clue.text: Odious brother an invalid

indicators.note: read as in-valid, not sound, signalling that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone finds their brother, who is unwell, detestable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' looks like a sick person but is the anagram signal, reworking BROTHER AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means hateful or repugnant, a close synonym of odious.

clue.text: Plenty tested out of bounds

indicators.note: the bounds of a word are its first and last letters, which are taken away

parts.note: to have sampled something is to have tested it

explanation.surface: Plenty of samples were checked beyond the permitted area.
explanation.walkthrough: SAMPLED loses its boundary letters S and D ('out of bounds').
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means more than enough, which is what plenty means.

clue.text: Farthest north tenants unusually modest

indicators.note: tenants occupy a property, so the north letter takes up residence inside
something done unusually departs from the normal order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: The tenants in the northernmost flats are remarkably unassuming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges MODEST into EDMOST, and N goes inside it after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means situated at the very end, the furthest away.

clue.text: Meantime, bury 'er other 'alf

parts.note: to inter a body is to bury it
a dropped-aitch rendering of her other half, her husband, said as 'im for him

explanation.surface: A Cockney widow says that for now she must bury her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H's mimic Cockney speech, so 'her other half' (him) becomes 'IM.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim is the time in between events, the meantime.

clue.text: Depressed and spitting feathers?

definitions.meaning: a jokey reading: someone spitting out feathers has fluff from a pillow between their lips

explanation.surface: Someone is feeling low and furious at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spitting feathers' is a British idiom for being very angry, which hides the literal sense: down (fine feathers) in someone's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means looking unhappy or dispirited, from the downturned corners of a sad face.

clue.text: Snakes wailed, exposed to the elements

parts.note: a road that snakes winds
to have wailed is to have wept

explanation.surface: Snakes hiss and moan when left out in the bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snakes' is a verb here, as a river or road snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Windswept describes a place open to strong winds, exposed to the weather.

clue.text: See 13
To listen to soft material, keeping time, can be profound

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the time letter sits between the two pieces

parts.note: to hear something is to listen to it
felt is a soft matted fabric

explanation.surface: Listening to a soft fabric, given time, can be a deep experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' has the two outer pieces hold the time letter between them; 'can be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt feelings are deep and sincere, which is what profound means here.

clue.text: Drugs can make you crazy

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine, a drug
a pot is a container, like a can

explanation.surface: A warning that taking drugs can drive you mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is a noun, a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person; used as an adjective it means mad.

clue.text: Skin disease revealed in phone call by creep

parts.note: to give someone a ring is to phone them
a worm is a contemptible person, a creep

explanation.surface: A dermatological complaint comes to light during a phone call from an unpleasant man.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringworm is a fungal infection that makes ring-shaped patches on the skin.

clue.text: Captivating women is tricky

indicators.note: something tricky is twisted or knotty, signalling a reshuffle of letters

explanation.surface: Charming women can be hard to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges the letters of WOMEN IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome means charming and appealing, a synonym of captivating.

clue.text: PM not working with Coalition's third image-maker

indicators.note: not signals that the working letters are taken away

parts.note: David Cameron was UK Prime Minister, heading a coalition government from 2010
on means working, as a machine that is on

indicators.note: the third letter of the word Coalition is wanted

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister, no longer active, sits with the coalition's third party as the face of the government.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMERON without ON leaves CAMER; the third letter of Coalition is A.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is a device that takes pictures, so it literally makes images.

clue.text: Lost without hour that used to be passed in pubs

definitions.text: that used to be passed in pubs

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for lost goes around the hour

parts.note: to go astray is to get lost

explanation.surface: Someone missing the time recalls how things went in pubs in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. The definition recalls the days before indoor smoking bans, when ashtrays went round pub tables.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashtray holds cigarette ash and was handed round pubs before smoking was banned indoors.

clue.text: Structure of sporting body with British in charge

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which governs English football

explanation.surface: A sports governing body is set up with a Briton at its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric can mean the basic framework of something, as in the fabric of society or of a building.

clue.text: This'll slay you: a wag less than sincere!

indicators.note: to wag is to shake to and fro, signalling that the letters are moved about
less than the whole word, so sincere loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A joker warns that his insincere quip will have you in stitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wag' looks like a joker but is the anagram signal; 'less than' cuts SINCERE to SINCER, which goes with A to give the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a deadly poison, so it is something that will kill you.

clue.text: Air-conditioned car crashing in capital

parts.note: AC is short for air-conditioned

indicators.note: a car crashing is wrecked, signalling its letters are broken up

explanation.surface: An air-conditioned car crashes in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' reshuffles the vehicle's letters into CRA; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: A believer or otherwise

parts.note: a theist believes in God

explanation.surface: Whether someone is a person of faith or not.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'or otherwise': the opposite of a believer is built by putting A before THEIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist rejects belief in God, the reverse of a believer.

clue.text: I made clear home help's back

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: back means the word for help is read in reverse

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Someone says they made it plain that the home help is back.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter I is spoken as a code word so that it is made clear over radio; 'back' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The phonetic alphabet word for the letter I removes ambiguity in radio messages.

clue.text: The ultimate in vitriolic about party's ideology

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the last one of vitriolic

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a do is a party; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Something deeply vitriolic is said about a political party's beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs or principles, a creed or ideology.

clue.text: Game make tracks by hilltop

parts.note: to make tracks is to leave, to part
a ridge is the long crest of a hill

explanation.surface: Hunters set off for some sport up near the hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link; Game here means birds shot for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a game bird, shot for sport and food.

clue.text: Actual model in cute hat

indicators.note: to model is to shape, signalling that the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A real fashion model sports a cute hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a fashion model but is a verb, to shape, rearranging IN CUTE HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic means genuine or real, the same as actual.

clue.text: Raising agent up until now without a message centre

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for up until now goes around the rest

parts.note: yet means up to the present time

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A recruiting agent has so far gone without receiving a message from head office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: YET goes round A and S, the centre of message.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast makes dough rise, so it is used as a raising agent in baking.
